title: Dependency stitch: quiet-window + burn-in slate
body:
Summary:
This is a working slate for a dependency-first release we want to run inside a quiet window. Goal: migrate auth-proxy v1 -> v2 and the routing sidecar across live Dedicated clusters with minimal customer impact. Primary concerns: cold-starts, KV-cache warming, circuit-breaker thresholds, and cross-service contract mismatches.

High-level approach (why different):
- Treat the dependency migration as the release driver (not the feature change).
- Enforce a burn-in phase (traffic=0 but golden canaries running) to validate memory/GC & connection spikes for 72h before any traffic ramp.
- Use telemetry gates that combine latency P50/P95, error rate, and KV hit-rate, not just server health.

Micro-calendar (quiet window plan) -- in this doc we keep small windows to reduce blast radius: 
- Day -7: Notify SRE owners, populate watchlist, tag relevant dashboards.
- Day -3: Deploy canary artifacts to canary fleet (no traffic). Start burn-in: run synthetic workloads, model calls, embedding mixes.
- Day -2: Review burn-in telemetry; run dependency contract tests (consumer->provider harness).
- Day 0 (quiet window 0200-0500 PT):
  * 02:00 - baseline snapshot + DB read-only isolation check
  * 02:10 - roll auth-proxy v2 to 1% of nodes (control-plane roll)
  * 02:25 - run smoke-gen tests at 1% (latency + correctness)
  * 02:40 - if green, bump to 5% and run KV warmup scripts (prefetch common prefixes)
  * 03:10 - telemetry gate decision point A (P50 <= baseline+20ms, errors < 0.1% above baseline, KV hit-rate >= 65%)
  * 03:30 - if pass, 20% ramp; 04:15 - gate B (same metrics with stricter thresholds); 04:45 - 50% ramp; then 05:00 - final 100% cutover or schedule backfill step
- Day +1 to +3: heightened observation, staggered backfills for slow clients, adjust traffic-shaping policies.

Preflight checklist (must be green before any day-0 action):
- [ ] Release artifact built & SHA verified (infra/CI job id: CI-2219)
- [ ] Baseline dashboards saved (link in linked_artifacts)
- [ ] Rollback image prepared & smoke-tested on staging
- [ ] SLI baseline recorded for the past 14 days
- [ ] Canary fleet node quota reserved
- [ ] Pager rotation assigned and tested (contact matrix below)
- [ ] Legal/compliance not required for this minor infra change (confirmed with S. Gomez)
- [ ] Canaries have labels for tracing and distributed sampling enabled

Telemetry gates and thresholds (examples — tune at Day -3):
- Latency: P50 <= baseline + 20ms, P95 <= baseline + 100ms
- Errors: service error count (5xx) increase <= 0.1% absolute; if doubled from baseline, fail gate
- KV/cache hit-rate: global >= 65% (we expect cache warmup to improve this)
- CPU: node-level 95th percentile < 85% sustained for 5 minutes
- Queue latency: ingress queue < 200ms 99th

Canary ramp recipe (percent windows and checks):
- Burn-in (72h): no user traffic; synthetic golden path only. Verify memory leak absence, GC patterns stable.
- 0% -> 1% (10m): smoke tests + synthetic correctness
- 1% -> 5% (15m): warmup scripts (prefetch triggers), health checks
- 5% -> 20% (35m): run traffic shadow tests for non-critical routes, check telemetry gate A
- 20% -> 50% (45m): run spike test (QPS + 2x normal), validate latency tail
- 50% -> 100% (90m): controlled ramp with autoscaler watch; if any metric breaches, immediate rollback to previous stable set

Rollback matrix (quick):
- Trigger: P95 latency > baseline + 200ms for 10m OR error spike > 0.5% absolute for 5m
- Action levels:
  1) Automatic throttle: immediately reduce traffic to 20% of normal using rate limiter for 5m while triage begins
  2) Manual rollback: deploy prior image to affected pool, follow post-rollback check (verify P50/P95 back to baseline within 15m)
  3) Escalation: if rollback doesn't recover within 30m, open incident and activate cross-team bridge

Comms playbook (templates):
- Slack ops channel (ops-release):
  "@here starting auth-proxy v2 canary at 02:10 PT. Day-0 plan: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100%. Watchlist: latency/P95, 5xx, KV hit-rate. If you see anomalies, add +triage and ping @oncall-release. Linked artifacts: JIRA-5821, PR#789"
- Customer-facing blurb (to CS/AMs pre-quiet window):
  "Planned minor platform maintenance in quiet window 02:00-05:00 PT to deploy an infra component (auth-proxy). We do not expect customer-visible downtime; reduced risk windows chosen to limit impact. If there are regressions we'll pause and rollback. Contact success@redwood.com in case of customer escalations."

Runbook shortcuts & commands (ops cheat sheet):
- Promote rollback: infractl deploy --image auth-proxy:v1 --target pool-canaries --wait 900
- Snapshot logs for time window: logpull --from 2026-04-10T02:00Z --to 2026-04-10T05:00Z --labels auth-proxy,canary > canary-logs-04010
- Quick KV hitrate: metrics query "kv_cache_hit_rate{service=\"auth-proxy\"}" last_5m

Observability checklist (dashboards & alerts):
- Primary dashboard: auth-proxy/latency-tail + distributed-trace-sampler (saved view)
- Secondary: kv-cache heatmap, connection churn, threadpool-saturation
- Alerts to mute during burn-in: synthetic-endpoint-failure (we'll get noise from golden tests) — instead rely on operational gate alerts listed above

Post-release retro template (to fill in during Day +3 retro):
- What went well (notes):
- What surprised us (notes):
- Telemetry misses / gaps (what we didn't track):
- Action items with owners (short list):

Open questions / TODOs before Day -3:
- Should we expand burn-in payload to include embedding-heavy flows? (Priya)
- Add consumer contract injected faults at 0%, confirm graceful degradations (Evan)
- Confirm KMS rotation will not coincide with Day 0 in region eu-west-1 (Derek to confirm)

Notes to self (personal):
- Keep quiet-window short but dense; we can afford multiple micro-windows on consecutive days instead of one long outage.
- Bring extra coffee for the 02:00 watch.

Appendix: quick references
- Consumer contract test script: tools/contract-harness/consumer-check.sh (run locally against canary)
- Synthetic load harness: https://ci.redwood-infra/synthetics/job/warp-48h
- Oncall rotation: ops-release on-call map (linked in confluence)

-- end of draft slate --

If you are editing this doc: keep notes inline, mark any changes with initials and date (e.g., "AP 2026-04-02: added KV gate threshold suggestions"). This is intentionally terse — final release brief will be produced once burn-in completes and Day -2 checks are green.
